title: Fallback Variant Negotiator and Standby Acceptance Suite
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Problem: During region failovers we need deterministic, low-risk fallbacks that both preserve latency SLOs and execution unit cost. Existing warm-standby checks focus on fleet liveness and basic KV population but do not negotiate compatible model variants or actively weigh tier/cost trade-offs when choosing fallback routes. This ticket implements two complementary pieces: (1) a Fallback Variant Negotiator service that decides, per-request or per-route, which compatible model variant to use when the primary model cannot be served in the selected region or tier (considering quantization, seq-len, latency headroom, and per-token cost); and (2) a Standby Acceptance Suite: a repeatable automated test harness and gating criteria that certifies warm standbys are "acceptance-ready" before they are used in failover (includes KV prefill verification, prefix cache health, and synthetic request replay to validate QoE and cost delta).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Negotiator returns a ranked list of compatible fallback variants with metadata (latency_estimate_ms, cost_delta_pct, accuracy_penalty_estimate) for >95% of simulated request traces. 2) Standby Acceptance Suite computes standby_readiness_score and requires >=0.92 to mark standby as ready. 3) KV prefill verification reports kv_fill_ratio >= 0.85 over target prefixes. 4) Synthetic replay P50 latency on standby <= primary_P50 * 1.25 for 95th percentile of traces. 5) End-to-end failover drills using canary traffic succeed with no customer-facing errors and failover_success_rate >= 0.995 across 1000 synthetic requests.
implementation_notes: - Implement lightweight capability descriptor exchange between serving runtime and negotiator (JSON proto). - Use existing kernel/quantization compatibility table and expand to include expected tokenization differences and seq-length sensitivity. - Add cost model hooks that compute expected per-token compute units for candidate variants. - Standby Acceptance Suite runs in a namespaced lab cluster and produces readiness artifacts stored in S3 for audit and rollbacks.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for negotiator ranking logic and cost model calibration. 2) Integration test: simulate region outage and assert negotiator selects fallback with acceptable latency/cost trade-off. 3) Acceptance Suite: run kv-prefill checker, prefix cache validation, and synthetic replay harness across 3 standby clusters (eu-west, us-east, ap-south) and publish readiness_score. 4) Canary rollout: route 0.5% of production traffic through a negotiated fallback variant in a non-critical org, observe metrics for 24h.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Create metrics: fallback_choice_latency_ms, negotiator_ranking_hits, standby_readiness_score, kv_fill_ratio, synthetic_replay_p50_ms, failover_success_rate. Add dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/standby-readiness and alert: standby_readiness_score < 0.88 for >10m.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy negotiator and acceptance-suite to staging and run overnight synthetic exercises (2 days). Phase 2: gated canary in staging-like orgs with 0.5% traffic (7 days). Phase 3: enable negotiator for auto-fallback in non-critical regions; ops will monitor readiness_score and rollback if alerts fire. Phase 4: full enablement after 2 weeks of stable canary data and incident postmortem.
rollback_plan: Revert negotiator routing rules and mark affected standbys as DQ (disqualified) in routing table. Promote manual routing to primary model for affected orgs. Restore previous failover controller image. Post-rollback diagnostics: dump negotiator decision traces and synthetic replay logs.
notes: Focus on determinism: negotiator decisions must be reproducible given the same capability descriptors and request signature to aid debugging. Minimize runtime overhead by caching recent negotiation results keyed by model variant, seq-length bucket, and region.
